network.title: The network, live
network.subtitle: Faithful simulation of the BitChat protocol parameters (whitepaper v2.0, public domain): controlled flooding with TTL and jitter, "spray-and-wait" couriers to reach a peer out of range.
network.archiBodyB: (local range, multi-hop, zero infrastructure) then falls back to the
network.archiBodyC: (VPS bridge `/api/mesh/bridge` + real-time relay, geohash channels) when no one is in range. The router picks the best transport automatically — here, the local "courier" queue plays the store-and-forward role.
network.cryptoTitle: Encryption: Noise XX in session, Noise X offline
network.cryptoBodyB: (Curve25519, ChaCha20-Poly1305): mutual authentication and forward secrecy. Offline mail is sealed in
network.cryptoBodyC: toward the recipient's static key — relays only carry opaque ciphertext. This demo implements the WebCrypto equivalent: ECDH P-256 + AES-GCM 256.
network.storeBodyA: Four mechanisms cover "the recipient isn't there": the sender's persistent outbox, the
network.storeBodyB: (3 carrier peers, copy budget 4→8, daily rotating tags), public history reconciliation via Golomb filters (GCS) every 15 s, and the
network.geohashTitle: Geohash channels: the map becomes a social space
network.geohashBody: A geohash encodes lat/lng into nestable cells: 7 characters = a block (~150 m), 5 = a city (~5 km), 2 = a country. Each cell is a public room carried by the relays; identities are ephemeral per zone.
network.metaBody: The whitepaper says it itself: the peer ID is stable and announcements publish keys in the clear — a radio observer can track a device across space and time. Rotating identities are listed as "future work". And on the demo side: the static-static ECDH of DMs offers no forward secrecy (no prekeys). Full transparency.
